description: The system notification an app posts when a chat finishes a turn or asks you something while you're elsewhere (the system's own banner, not drawn in the window): the picture on the left, the chat's name as its first line, what happened under it.
opens: a chat's turn ends or it asks a question or needs a permission answer, while its window is not in front or another chat is open

parts.name: Picture
parts.shows: On the left. For a Bot: its picture, round, with the app's logo in its bottom-right corner cut out of it (tokens notification.*); for any other chat, or a Bot with no picture: the app's logo. On macOS the icon is the app it's posted as: Baude's or Record's notifier (an app of its own, built and signed on the Mac), whose icon is the app's logo, with a Bot's picture, round and without the logo, attached on the right; where there's no notifier yet, or macOS won't let it post, the notification is osascript's and its icon Script Editor's, with no picture. On the phone the logo is the notification's small icon and the Bot's picture its large one.

parts.name: Title
parts.shows: The first line: the chat's name, for the open chat the window's title; for a Bot, its name, never its chat's title; for any other chat, its title ("(untitled)" if it has none). Never the app's name: the system shows which app it is.

parts.name: Body
parts.shows: Under the title, up to two lines (no subtitle between): what happened, the reply's first words when a turn finishes ("Finished" when there is nothing to say), "Waiting for your answer: <tool>", or "Claude has a question for you".

actions.does: Brings the window up with that chat open (a chat on a host has its transcript fetched first).

The same as a click. A click on one posted before the app restarted, or by another of its processes, opens that chat in the window you were in last (a local chat's, by its session id). Once the app has quit, a click or Open starts the app on that chat (a local chat: --cwd, --resume).

states.name: a Bot switched away from, mid-turn
states.shows: Its notification, titled with the Bot's name, when its turn ends or it waits.

states.name: its turn's end seen on another head
states.shows: Gone, on every head of the mesh: once any head shows the turn's end on screen (a Baude window in front on that chat with its chat tab shown, a Record window in front reading it, the phone's app in front on its chat page), that head tells the chat's host (seen), the host lists it seen to every head, and each takes its notification of that turn's end back: macOS through the notifier's withdraw (Notification Center's removeDeliveredNotifications by its identifier, the chat's key), Linux through org.freedesktop.Notifications' CloseNotification by its id (or GLib's withdraw_notification), Android through NotificationManager.cancel by its tag (chat:<host>/<chat>), whether the app's in front, put away, or ended by Android with only the notification left (SeenJob reaches the host again). One whose turn's end was seen before it was to be posted isn't posted.

decisions.said: Replies that finish in the background should notify through the OS's notification system, not only the sidebar's dots
decisions.rule: Every app posts the platform's own notification when a chat finishes a turn or asks something while you're elsewhere (Settings → Notifications).

decisions.said: Notifications waste space: the app's name on line one, the chat's name on line two and the problem cut short on line three. The left should show Baude's logo, or the Bot's picture with Baude's in its corner; the first line the chat's name; the description under it, up to two lines.
decisions.rule: Every app's notification is the picture (a Bot's with the app's logo in its corner, else the app's logo), the chat's or Bot's name as the title and what happened as the body, with no subtitle and no line for the app's own name.

decisions.said: Notifications look fine implement that. / Self signed cert and just bundle docs on how people can safely sign Baude
decisions.rule: On macOS each app posts through a notifier app of its own, built on the Mac and signed with a self-signed code-signing certificate that tools/macos-sign.sh makes in a keychain of its own (docs/macos-signing.md); without one, or turned away, it posts through osascript.

decisions.said: If I see a bot message anywhere on the mesh, the notification should disappear / Specificlly, the notiifaction shoulddisappear from my phone
decisions.rule: A chat's turn's-end notification is taken back on every head of the mesh (the phone's first: in front, put away, or ended by Android) as soon as any head shows that turn's end on screen in a window that's in front or the phone's app in front; one seen before it's posted is never shown. Each notification is known by its chat and its turn's end (the uuid of the message it ended with, and its transcript's size then).
